field_conventions.steps: Each step is {action, time_s, time_s_max}. time_s is the single time or the low end of a range; time_s_max is the high end of a range or null. Non-timed actions (vent, stir) have time_s null.
field_conventions.reference_wattage_w: Wattage the label says the directions were developed for. null when the label gives a wattage table instead of one reference, or when no wattage is stated.
field_conventions.wattage_variants: Explicit per-wattage times printed on the label, as [{wattage_w, time_s, time_s_max, note}].
field_conventions.instructions_completeness: complete = reference wattage or wattage table plus timed steps from a label transcription; partial = times present but wattage and/or steps missing; none = no microwave directions found; not_applicable = label says do not microwave or the product is oven only.
field_conventions.upc: Only recorded when shown on a source page. Never computed. Retailer-specific item IDs are not UPCs and are kept in retailer_item_id.

notes: 33 products: frozen_tray 14, cup_bowl 8, steam_bag 6, pouch 2, oven_only 3. Brands chosen are national brands sold at Safeway, Vons, Ralphs, Albertsons, Target and Walmart in California, but shelf presence was not checked store by store.

Main source was SmartLabel (smartlabel.labelinsight.com), which carries label transcriptions for Conagra brands (Banquet, Healthy Choice, Marie Callender's, Hungry-Man, Birds Eye, Frontera) and B&G Foods (Green Giant). These pages give UPC, net weight and full step-by-step directions. The /nutrition subpage gives serving data but returned server errors for some products.

Retailer pages that were readable: H-E-B (heb.com, nutrition plus short directions, no UPC), Safeway /shop/pd/ URLs (full directions, no UPC), preview.hannaford.com (full directions plus tray material), Wegmans and ShopRite (nutrition, UPC on ShopRite). Blocked or empty: Walmart, Target, Kroger/Ralphs (JS shell), Safeway/Albertsons product-details URLs (Incapsula), Publix, Lowes Foods, the main Hannaford/Stop & Shop/Food Lion/Giant sites (all in maintenance), Open Food Facts (robots disallowed, curl blocked by proxy), and the leancuisine.com, stouffers.com and amys.com product pages.

Nestle brands (Lean Cuisine, Stouffer's, DiGiorno) and Amy's, Kraft Heinz, Hormel, Campbell's, Nissin, Maruchan and Mars (Ben's Original) are not on the labelinsight SmartLabel host, so their records rely on retailer copies and are more often partial and missing UPC.

No source stated a resin identification code (recycling number) for any tray, cup or bowl. Only the Lean Cuisine page described material (uncolored plastic tray, recyclable where accepted), Nissin's cup is paper per news coverage, Marie Callender's pot pies use paperboard trays, and Ben's Original pouches are described as BPA-free. Container material will have to come from photographs of the packages.

Explicit wattage tables appear mainly on steam bags (Birds Eye: 1200/1000/800 W with stovetop below 800 W; Green Giant: 1200/1000/700 W or 1000 W plus 700 W). Conagra frozen trays use a single 1100 W reference with no low-wattage times. Marie Callender's single-serve pot pies say microwaves below 1100 W are not recommended, which is a useful rule for the app's wattage logic.

Do-not-microwave cases found: Maruchan Instant Lunch cup ('Do not microwave', hot water only) and Tyson raw stuffed chicken cordon bleu ('DO NOT MICROWAVE OR AIR FRY', 'Oven bake only, raw chicken'). The reverse case also exists: Healthy Choice Power Bowls say DO NOT cook in conventional or toaster ovens. DiGiorno only has oven directions, but no explicit do-not-microwave wording was found online.

A UK Sainsbury's listing for Ben's Original Jasmine microwave rice (220 g) gives 2 min at 700 W or 90 s at 900 W with squeeze and tear-corner steps. It is a different market and package, so it was not merged into the US records. The US pouch directions should be photographed.

Retailer-transcribed directions (Safeway, H-E-B) can be abridged. H-E-B often gives only a total time in the description while its Instructions field is empty. Records built from these are marked partial or flagged.

UPC formats differ by source: SmartLabel gives 12-digit UPC-A; ShopRite shows a 14-digit GTIN with leading zeros; Campbell's Foodservice shows an 11-digit form. Values are stored exactly as shown and flagged for confirmation against the package barcode.
Healthy Choice Power Bowl Spicy Steak Burrito reports 180 kcal for 262 g on SmartLabel. This was recorded as found but should be checked on the package.

Packaging and recipes change. Cup Noodles moved from polystyrene to a microwavable paper cup in 2024, and older stock may differ. Treat every record as a seed to be confirmed against the photographed package.
